eyebrow: AI Engineering Leadership & Architecture · Chapter Four
subtitle: Lesson 17 · From One Fix to a Standard Everyone Follows

eyebrow: Why an announced standard often gets ignored
code:
A Slack link to a new "standards" doc, with no
follow-up, rarely changes behavior.

Reading a document and changing a habit
are different things -- the announcement
doesn't close that gap.
caption: Under time pressure, people default back to whatever they were already doing.

code:
Human-enforced:
  "Make sure every ADR lists alternatives."
  -- followed inconsistently. Reviewers are busy.

Tooling-enforced:
  A CI check fails the PR if that section is missing.
  -- followed consistently. No one has to remember.
caption: Wherever a standard CAN be enforced by tooling, it should be.

eyebrow: Introducing a standard without imposing it
code:
Handed down as a finished document
  -> followed resentfully, or not at all.

Bring the PROBLEM to the team first:
  "We've had three incidents now where test data
   didn't match production -- should we fix that?"
  -> a standard the team helped design.
caption: A standard the team helped design is a standard the team has ownership of.

code:
Hard requirement
  Every deploy requires an automated test pass.
  No exceptions -- the cost of slipping is high.

Strong default
  Design docs should typically be under 5 pages.
  Followed almost always -- but a conscious,
  explained exception is fine.
caption: Zero room for judgment produces workarounds, not compliance.
